final_message:
The bug was in `recover` in `billing/dunning.py`. After a retry paid the invoice, the subscription stayed `past_due`.

`recover` is supposed to return a `past_due` or `unpaid` subscription to `active` once nothing else is outstanding. Its `if not outstanding:` branch contained only `pass`, so the subscription never changed state. I replaced `pass` with `transition(ctx, subscription, "active")`.

Your reproduction test now passes when run on its own, and the existing suite still passes (24 tests). I didn't add the test to the suite; I ran it from a temporary file and deleted it afterwards.

I wrote `answer.json` in the repository root as `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && grep -n "past_due\|retry\|def " engine.py | head -80
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py && sed -n 50,75p engine.py && grep -n "def \|status" subscriptions.py | head -60
cat dunning.py payments.py && sed -n 50,75p engine.py && grep -n "def \|status" subscriptions.py | head -60

sed -i 's/^        pass$/        transition(ctx, subscription, "active")/' dunning.py && tail -4 dunning.py && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}' > ../answer.json && cd .. && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}' > ../answer.json && cd .. && cat >> tests/test_recovery_tmp.py <<'EOF'
EOF
rm tests/test_recovery_tmp.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat answer.json; cat > tests/test_tmp.py <<'EOF'
def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_tmp.py 2>&1 | tail -3; rm tests/test_tmp.py
